Detailed Task / What the New Joinee Will:
1. Role Mapping: Map Well-being responsibilities against Mentor, SC, TL, Principal, teacher and external professionals.

2. Boundary Casebook: Respond to 8–10 situations involving confidentiality, student requests, parents, teachers, academic concerns, behaviour and wellbeing.

3. Confidentiality & Escalation: Given 5 scenarios, identify what can remain confidential, what must be shared and with whom.

4. Professional Practice Statement: Create a one-page personal set of professional non-negotiables.
Input / Resource: Counselor Training Manual – Section I; school JD; confidentiality/safeguarding SOPs; discussion with TL
Measurable Criteria: Correctly identifies scope and boundaries; makes appropriate confidentiality/escalation decisions; no critical error in safeguarding/confidentiality scenarios
Evidence / Output: Role map; completed scenarios; practice statement; discussion notes
Discussion Points:
- SOP for which concerns would be taken by whom and when (DC/SC/CC).
- Whom to be kept in loop.

Detailed Task / What the New Joinee Will:
1. Understand the Well-being Pyramid: Classroom guidance → Intentional Guidance → Individual Support → Specialised Intervention.

2. JS Referral Process: Work through the complete referral pathway using a case.

3. SS Referral Process: Work through teacher, parent and student referral routes.

4. Referral Decision Lab: Respond to 8–10 different cases and decide: monitor / intervene / collaborate / refer / escalate.

5. Stakeholder Map: Identify who needs to be involved at each stage.
Input / Resource: Current Counselor Training Manual; JS & SS referral flowcharts; intervention forms; external referral process
Measurable Criteria: Demonstrates understanding of purpose and sequence; ≥80% appropriate referral decisions; correctly identifies stakeholders and escalation points
Evidence / Output: Completed referral case sheets; stakeholder map; system practice; viva
Discussion Points: - Actual case in presence of the previous counselor. Fill observation after it (to be taken seriously).

Detailed Task / What the New Joinee Will:
1. Nucleus Navigation: Locate intervention forms, counselor entry forms, case history and relevant records.

2. Case Entry: Complete a case record using an actual case, after it has been reviewed and approved by the TL.
Input / Resource: Nucleus; FSApps; Counselor Entry Forms; annual counseling folder/SOP
Measurable Criteria: Can independently locate and use required systems; documentation is objective, relevant, confidential and complete
Evidence / Output: Mock Nucleus entry; case note; audit; case tracker
SM's Comments: This would need to be updated because of new changes in the session/meeting format

Detailed Task / What the New Joinee Will:
1. Structured Observation: Observe 2 students across different contexts.

2. Student Voice Conversation: Conduct a structured conversation to understand the student's perspective.

3. Stakeholder Conversation: Speak with relevant teacher/Mentor/MOM to gather contextual information.

4. Case Formulation: Record strengths, presenting concern, patterns, possible contributing factors, protective factors, assumptions and missing information.

5. Formulation Conference: Present the case to the TL and revise based on feedback.
Input / Resource: Observation formats; Nucleus; Counselor Handbook; experienced counselor modelling
Measurable Criteria: Distinguishes observation from interpretation; seeks multiple perspectives; identifies missing information; avoids premature conclusions/labels
Evidence / Output: 2 structured observations; student voice record; case formulation; revised version

Detailed Task / What the New Joinee Will:
1. Observe 5 Counseling Sessions: Each observation has a specific focus rather than generic reflection: session structure, listening, questioning, intervention and closure/follow-up.

2. Micro-Skills Practice: Practise paraphrasing, summarising, reflecting emotion, open questioning and use of silence.

3. Role Plays: Reluctant student; defensive/angry student; emotionally overwhelmed student; "I don't know" student; student seeking direct advice.

4. Real Student Session – Attempt 1: Conduct session under observation.

5. Feedback & Reattempt: Re-conduct with 2–3 specific improvement goals.

6. Reflection: Identify what was missed, what was assumed and what changed after feedback.
Input / Resource: Counselor's Handbook; 5 observed sessions; counseling plans; selected video/resources; experienced counselor modelling
Measurable Criteria: Demonstrates rapport, active listening, appropriate questioning, empathy, summarising, boundaries, student agency and purposeful closure; demonstrates improvement after feedback
Evidence / Output: Observation sheets; role-play rubric; observed session 1 & 2; reflection

Detailed Task / What the New Joinee Will:
1. Goal Setting: Define what change/progress would look like.

2. Implement: Conduct at least one supervised intervention/session.

3. Follow-up: Review progress with the student and relevant stakeholders.

4. Re-plan: Modify intervention where evidence suggests it is not working.

5. Closure/Referral Decision: Decide whether to continue, modify, close or refer and justify the decision.
Input / Resource: Counseling plan format; case discussion with TL; current referral SOP
Measurable Criteria: Intervention is linked to case formulation; goals are clear; follow-up occurs; decision to continue/modify/close/refer is justified
Evidence / Output: Intervention plan; session record; follow-up record; closure/referral rationale

Detailed Task / What the New Joinee Will:
1. Observe 2 Adult Meetings: One teacher/Mentor meeting and one parent meeting.

2. Teacher Consultation Role Play: Discuss a concern without diagnosing or labelling the student.

3. Parent Meeting Role Play: Parent asks for diagnosis, immediate action or guarantee.

4. Difficult Parent Case: Parent disagrees with the counselor's recommendation.

5. External Referral Simulation: Explain why referral is recommended, the process and the counselor's continuing role.
Input / Resource: Referral SOP; parent communication protocols; external psychologist/therapist referral process
Measurable Criteria: Communicates objectively; protects confidentiality; maintains boundaries; does not overpromise/diagnose; identifies when external support is required
Evidence / Output: Meeting observation forms; role-play rubric; referral simulation

Detailed Task / What the New Joinee Will:
1. Observe 2 Life Classes: Ideally one JS and one SS experience where applicable.

2. Understand Needs Assessment: Examine how student/teacher needs inform topics.

3. Design One Life Class: Objective, activity, facilitation plan, student engagement and evidence of learning.

4. Rehearse: Conduct session for TL/team.

5. Feedback & Redesign: Make improvements based on feedback.

6. Deliver/Co-facilitate: Conduct an actual Life Class where appropriate.

7. Evaluate: Collect evidence of student/teacher response and reflect.
Input / Resource: PSPE Scope & Sequence; existing Life Class plans; needs assessment; current Life Class process
Measurable Criteria: Session has clear purpose, age appropriateness and meaningful student engagement; facilitator can adapt rather than simply follow a script
Evidence / Output: 2 observation records; session plan; rehearsal feedback; revised plan; actual delivery evidence
Discussion Points:
- Either JS and SS or two different grades.
- One session in MLC cohort can be conducted.

Detailed Task / What the New Joinee Will:
1. Counselor Handbook: Identify 3 principles and demonstrate where they apply in practice.

2. Selected Counseling Modules: Work through at least 5 relevant modules and discuss application with TL.

3. Video/Case Resource: Analyse a counseling demonstration for specific counselor behaviours rather than generic reflection.

4. FS Teacher Training Toolbox: Complete selected relevant topics such as sexuality education, learning disabilities, cyber safety and POCSO.

5. Reading: Use selected resources such as Dibs / Tarshi books as supporting professional learning.
Input / Resource: Counselor's Handbook; counseling modules; FS Teacher Training Toolbox; selected books/videos
Measurable Criteria: Can connect learning resource to actual practice; demonstrates understanding through discussion/application rather than submission of a reflection alone
Evidence / Output: Application notes; discussion record; selected resource tasks
Discussion Points: Content that are not relevant can be removed and re-worked.

Training Topic: 10. Final Professional Readiness Demonstration - Graduation Presentation
Detailed Task / What the New Joinee Will:
1. Complete Professional Case Cycle: Referral/concern → information gathering → student voice → formulation → goal → intervention → collaboration → documentation → follow-up → outcome → closure/next step.

2. Final Observed Session: Conduct an independent session with an actual student where appropriate.

3. Case Conference: Present and defend professional decisions.

4. Complex Case Simulation: Respond to an unexpected development/change in the case.

5. Readiness Viva: Scenario-based questions covering role, boundaries, intervention and referral.

6. Professional Reflection: Based on overall learning lead a Graduation Presentation talking about possible strategies used or can be used by the team
Input / Resource: Entire training portfolio; case records; observation rubrics; referral SOP
Measurable Criteria: Demonstrates independent judgement, safe practice, effective counseling, appropriate documentation, collaboration and follow-through
Evidence / Output: Complete anonymised case portfolio; final observation; case presentation; simulation; viva; reflection
SM's Comments: To identify the presentation format and the stakeholders who will attend the presentation
Discussion Points:
- Based on your observations, what would you want to try in your class (or a session).
- Something the existing team can learn.
- Attend 1-2 MYP/DP graduation presentation to get an idea.
- Counselors, principals, grade coordinators can attend
